title: Rounding Decimals; Fraction and Decimal Conversions

teacherCues: Draw a place-value chart including decimal places.
Ask: 'What does each place to the right of the decimal point mean?'

hints: 9 is in the fourth decimal place.

confusionCorner.title: Watch out!
confusionCorner.body: Don't read the decimal part as a separate whole number. [[imp:Always attach the place value of the final digit.]]

blocks.title: 1. Decimal Place Value

explanation: [[kw:Decimal numbers]] are parts of a whole, written to the right of the decimal point.
Each place is 10 times smaller than the place to its left: tenths, hundredths, thousandths, ten-thousandths, etc.
To read a decimal, say the number as if it were whole, then add the place value of the last digit. Example: 0.0796 is 'seven hundred ninety-six ten-thousandths'.
A whole number with a decimal is read with 'and' for the decimal point. Example: 126.2864 is 'one hundred twenty-six and two thousand eight hundred sixty-four ten-thousandths'.

visuals.title: Place Value Chart
visuals.caption: Each place is 10 times smaller as you move right.

discoveryHook.scenario: A bag of M&M's weighs 1.69 ounces. The '1' is a whole ounce; the '.69' means 69 hundredths of an ounce. The decimal point separates whole numbers from parts of a whole.

steps: Hundredths (cent) place is 6. Next digit is 3 (thousandths).
examples.title: A – Round to nearest cent

examples.prompt: Explain why $1{,}196.885$ rounded to the nearest cent is $1{,}196.89$.
examples.peerPrompt: What happens when the next digit is 5?
steps: The cent place is 8 (hundredths). The next digit is 5.
Since it's 5, round up the 8 to 9.
examples.title: B – When the next digit is exactly 5

steps: Tenths place is 6. Next digit is 4 (hundredths).
examples.title: C – Round to nearest tenth

teacherCues: Review whole-number rounding; note the only difference is dropping trailing zeros.
Emphasize: look at the digit to the right of the target place.

discoveryHook.scenario: The bag of M&M's contains 18 yellow candies out of 55: $\frac{18}{55} = 0.32727...$ This is a [[kw:repeating decimal]]. Rounded to the nearest hundredth, it's $0.33$. Rounding makes numbers manageable.

blocks.title: 2. Rounding Decimals

confusionCorner.body: Don't drop trailing zeros when rounding to a specific place. [[imp:If you round to hundredths, keep two decimal places even if the last digit is zero (e.g., 1.20).]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

challengeCorner.prompt: Round 0.9999 to the nearest thousandth. What do you notice?

visuals.title: Rounding Decimals Examples
visuals.caption: If the next digit is 5 or more, round up; then drop the rest.

explanation: Rounding decimals follows the same rules as whole numbers: [[imp:1. Identify the rounding digit. 2. Look right: if ≥5, round up; else keep. 3. Drop all digits to the right.]]
When rounding to nearest dollar, round to the ones place. Nearest cent means hundredths place.
Example: Round $166.39$ to nearest dollar: $166$ (tenths digit 3 < 5).
Round $1{,}196.885$ to nearest cent: hundredths digit 8, next digit 5 → round up → $1{,}196.89$.

questions.prompt: To round a decimal, look at the digit to the ___ of the target place.

hints: Cent = hundredths. The digit is 9, next 5 → round up, carry.

blocks.title: 3. Converting Fractions and Mixed Numbers to Decimals

challengeCorner.prompt: Convert $\frac{5}{11}$ to a decimal rounded to the nearest thousandth.

confusionCorner.title: Watch out!
confusionCorner.body: Not all fractions become nice, terminating decimals. [[imp:Some are repeating decimals; you may need to round to a specified place.]]

questions.prompt: To convert a fraction to a decimal, divide the ___ by the denominator.

explanation: To convert a proper fraction to a decimal: [[imp:Divide the numerator by the denominator. Add decimal point and zeros as needed.]]
For mixed numbers: either convert to improper fraction and divide, or divide the fraction part and add to the whole number.
$\frac{3}{8} \rightarrow 3 \div 8 = 0.375$.
Some fractions produce [[kw:repeating decimals]], like $\frac{18}{55} = 0.3272727...$

visuals.title: Fraction to Decimal Conversions
visuals.caption: Division of numerator by denominator gives the decimal form.

teacherCues: Show how the fraction bar means division.
For mixed numbers, convert to improper fraction or add whole to decimal.

discoveryHook.scenario: In a bag of 55 M&M's, 18 are yellow. The fraction $\frac{18}{55}$ equals 18 divided by 55 = 0.32727... Converting a fraction to a decimal is just dividing the numerator by the denominator.

examples.peerPrompt: You can do it in two steps.
examples.title: B – Mixed number conversion
examples.prompt: Explain how to convert $3\frac{2}{5}$ to a decimal.

steps: Write as 0.666... or rounded 0.67 (to nearest hundredth).
examples.title: C – Repeating decimal

discoveryHook.scenario: A bag of M&M's weighs 1.69 ounces. The .69 part is sixty-nine hundredths, or $\frac{69}{100}$. To convert a decimal to a fraction, write the decimal part over its place value, then reduce if possible.

teacherCues: Read the decimal in words to identify the denominator.

examples.title: A – Convert pure decimal
steps: Reduce: divide numerator and denominator by 125 → $\frac{7}{8}$.
examples.prompt: Convert 0.875 to a fraction in lowest terms.

examples.peerPrompt: Think: What happens when you divide 1 by 3?
examples.prompt: Why can't 0.333... be written as an exact fraction with denominator 10, 100, or 1,000?
steps: 0.333... is a repeating decimal, so it's not an exact number of tenths, hundredths, etc.
It can be expressed as $\frac{1}{3}$ exactly, but not as a terminating decimal fraction.
We use the fraction $\frac{1}{3}$ to represent it exactly.
examples.title: B – Converting a repeating decimal

examples.prompt: Convert 4.08 to a mixed number in lowest terms.
examples.title: C – Convert mixed decimal

blocks.title: 4. Converting Decimals to Fractions

confusionCorner.body: Don't forget to reduce the fraction to lowest terms. [[imp:Always simplify the fraction part after converting.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

challengeCorner.prompt: Convert 0.0625 to a fraction in lowest terms.

questions.prompt: To convert a decimal to a fraction, the denominator comes from the ___ value of the last digit.
Convert 0.45 to a fraction in lowest terms.
Convert 3.125 to a mixed number in lowest terms.

explanation: To convert a decimal to a fraction: [[imp:1. Write the decimal digits as the numerator. 2. Write the place value of the last digit as the denominator (e.g., .69 → hundredths → 100). 3. Reduce if possible.]]
For a mixed decimal (whole + decimal), write the decimal part as a fraction and keep the whole number.
Pure decimals (no whole part): e.g., $0.8 = \frac{8}{10} = \frac{4}{5}$.
Mixed decimals: e.g., $2.25 = 2\frac{25}{100} = 2\frac{1}{4}$.

visuals.title: Decimal to Fraction Conversions
visuals.caption: The denominator matches the last decimal place.

blocks.title: 5. Rounding in Fraction/Decimal Context

challengeCorner.prompt: A store has a sale: 'Buy two, get one half off.' The original price is \$15.99. What is the average cost per item if you buy three? Round to nearest cent.

teacherCues: Review both rounding and fraction-to-decimal conversion.
Show that fractions can be rounded by first converting to decimal, then rounding.

examples.title: A – Fraction to rounded decimal
examples.prompt: Express $\frac{5}{12}$ as a decimal rounded to the nearest thousandth.
steps: Thousandths place digit is 6; next digit (ten-thousandths) is 6 (≥5), so round up to 7.

examples.prompt: When is it better to use a fraction instead of a rounded decimal?
steps: Fractions are exact when dividing a whole into equal parts.
Rounded decimals may introduce small errors when used in further calculations.
Use fractions for exact amounts; use rounded decimals for approximations and reports.
examples.title: B – When to round vs. keep fraction
examples.peerPrompt: Think about exactness in measurements or recipes.

examples.prompt: Order $\frac{1}{6}$, $\frac{2}{11}$, and $\frac{3}{16}$ from highest to lowest by converting to decimals rounded to hundredths.
examples.title: C – Convert and round multiple fractions

confusionCorner.body: When rounding fractions to decimals, always round only at the final step, not intermediate steps. [[imp:Carry enough decimal places during division to avoid rounding errors.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

explanation: To express a fraction as a rounded decimal: convert the fraction to a decimal, then apply rounding rules to the required place.
Example: $\frac{7}{12} = 0.58333...$ rounded to hundredths → $0.58$ (since thousandths digit is 3).
For comparison, rounding to different places can change the precision. Always note the rounding instruction.
[[imp:Decimals with repeating digits must be rounded unless the exact fraction is required.]]

visuals.caption: Convert, then round to the desired place.
